claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features proximity voice chat that cuts off abruptly, which enhances the horror and comedic moments.

citations.review_text: Lethal Company is a game that is enjoyed with friends. Even better if you all have no idea what you're doing, or don't care what you're doing. It is hilarious if you have the capacity to joke and mess around. The proximity chat also amplifies the whole experience as well. I love it for being funny and a great time with friends.

This is honestly the gold standard for horror co-op. Nothing beats the absolute panic of trying to haul a heavy piece of scrap back to the ship while some unseen freak is chasing you down a dark hallway. The proximity chat is what makes it a complete masterpiece - hearing your friend's voice abruptly cut off mid-sentence as a Bracken snaps their neck in the dark never fails to make me cry laughing. 

We run a ton of modpacks and coordinate on our Discord server and it just takes the replay value to a whole new level. You can tweak the game to be genuinely terrifying, like straight out of an old-school slasher film, or completely absurd depending on what your crew is feeling that night. Whether you are sweating trying to meet the company quota or just goofing off and accidentally blowing each other up with landmines, it is easily some of the most fun I have ever had in a multiplayer game!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as best experienced when playing with friends, while playing solo is considered to strip away the charm or become sad and depressing.

citations.review_text: Sadly, this game has basically died by now. But, it still is a very goofy and fun game to play with friends, however I would not recommend buying this anymore if you have no friends to play it with.

Few games turn genuine horror into nonstop comedy quite as fast as this one. Dropping onto cursed industrial moons with a group of friends just to haul rusted bolts, clown horns, and giant axles back to the ship before nightfall creates hilarious chaos every single run.

The proximity voice chat is where the real magic happens. One second you are casually chatting with your buddy down a dark hallway, and the next second their voice cuts off mid sentence as a Bracken drags them into the shadows or they step straight onto a landmine. Between dodging giant eyeless dogs outside the ship, getting lost in maze like interiors, and watching everybody panic when the quota deadline hits, it is pure multiplayer gold. Playing solo strips away almost all the charm, yet with a crew on voice chat, it is easily one of the most entertaining co-op games out there.
Sad and depressing alone, but amazingly fun played with friends. No replication could do it justice. Intend to play for many more hours. Amaze, amaze, amaze. 10/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that official content updates are slow or infrequent.

citations.review_text: Lovely game. A bit boring when there isnt any new things being added very often. Would like to see a major update soon

The horror co-op game made by a roblox game maker that was so influential it birthed an entire genre of indie multiplayer co-op friend games, each with their own twist on the gameplay centered around having fun with the people you know. It is rare to get an indie game this good that also is low-end to run, which is likely why it is so successful, because it potato graphics so you can run it with a lemon and a battery, and its only 10 bucks. It has a graphical art style that is almost like a low resolution comic book game, but it nails it perfectly in a way the game is scary and immersive. It has strange lore that is so unique and interesting to dive into, despite limited knowledge. It is also immersive and fun for roleplaying. it is a strange game for not so strange people, anyone can enjoy it. It has phenomenal and endless mods too, so there is always something new to explore and test, even with the slow rate of official content updates. 
10/10 Icon. Extremely recommended
